verdict.rationale: Consensus markets a literature-review workflow to "search, screen, extract, and synthesize evidence." It documents per-paper extraction of PICO elements and study-design classification, study-type filters, and the Consensus Meter, which classifies each relevant paper against a yes/no question. Together with Deep Search and bulk library import, this gives a uniform automated pass over many papers. However, the evidence never shows user-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria or custom extraction fields applied consistently across a paper set, and all of it is vendor-claimed. Missing for 10: user-configurable screening criteria and custom extraction schema (e.g., extraction tables), a documented systematic-review workflow such as screening decisions or PRISMA-style tracking, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
